newsitem.title: CHINA: China top insurer sees premiums up 25 pct a year.
newsitem.headline: China top insurer sees premiums up 25 pct a year.

text.p: China's leading insurer, the People's Insurance Company of China (PICC), expects premium income to grow by 25.8 percent a year to the end of the century, state media said on Friday.
That would take premium income to 150 billion yuan ($18 billion) by 2000, an increase of 102.4 billion from the end of 1995, the China Daily said.
But PICC, China's sole insurer until 1988, would only be able to keep about 75 percent of the market, it said. The company held more than 79 percent of insurance business in China at the end of 1995.
The World Bank estimates China's booming insurance market will be worth around 2,000 billion yuan by the year 2000.
The target premium income includes 62 billion yuan from property insurance, 71 billion yuan from life insurance and 17 billion yuan from re-insurance, it said quoting company president Ma Yongwei.
Over the past years, PICC's life insurance income has lagged behind that generated from property insurance, he said.

"Chinese people will spend more money on life insurance, and more insurance products will be generated, with more and more of them becoming well-off," Xinhua news agency quoted PICC vice-president Wu Xiaoping as saying.
"There is great potential to be tapped in China's insurance market," he said.

PICC, which reorganised last July into a commercial limited liability enterprise that operates on market rules, earned premium income in 1996 of about 63.4 billion yuan in both domestic and overseas markets, up 25.2 percent from 1995.
Profits amounted to about 1.0 billion yuan ($120 million).

China now has 15 domestic and foreign insurers, including three nationwide companies and two foreign-funded insurers in Shanghai and southern Guangzhou. The number was growing, Xinhua said. PICC Life, one of PICC's three subsidiaries, earned 21.2 billion yuan in premium income last year, up 40 percent from 1995.
PICC Property earned 35 billion yuan last year, Xinhua said, adding only that PICC Reinsurance saw a stable increase in income. It gave no comparative figures.
